h1: DesignPro Academy — Education & Community Hero Section Design
tagline: Hero section reference built on black #000000 and teal #64CEFB, set in Inter and measured against 800x569.
summary: Hero section reference for an education or community brand — a dark stage, a 800x569 frame, React and Tailwind CSS and Inter.
about: DesignPro Academy shows one way to build the hero section for an education or community brand, and publishes the instructions that produced it. Colour is limited to black #000000 underneath, white #FFFFFF for the type and teal #64CEFB carrying the accents, set in Inter. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 800x569 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. If you are briefing a education hero section, start from this composition and replace the subject.

layout.title: Links collapse at one width
layout.body: The bar is the quietest part of the composition: wordmark, a short row of links and one #64CEFB action, all held at the smallest type step in the brief. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #64CEFB action is the only element in the bar with any weight.

layout.title: The type carries the tone
layout.body: The size steps and tracking in the brief are what give this its tone: Inter at a tight display size, then a clear drop to the supporting copy. The display face is used at one size only, so it never competes with itself. Do not add a size without a job.

layout.title: Navigation without a background
layout.body: The bar sits over the 800x569 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: The scale is the styling
layout.body: Numerals share the interface face, so statistics and labels belong to the same system.

motion.title: The controls are the interactive layer
motion.body: Feedback is limited to hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card, so the rest of the layout is a fixed composition. Each state changes one property, which keeps the feedback legible.

motion.title: Motion that stays out of the way
motion.body: There is no scroll library here: the 800x569 composition holds still and only the elements that respond to you move. There is no animation library in the brief, which keeps the rebuild small.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.weights: Weight not fixed in the brief
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

editorial.title: Why the education brief holds
editorial.body: Most education pages fail by adding: more sections, more gradients, more claims. DesignPro Academy goes the other way. The composition stays on black #000000 with teal #64CEFB for actions, which is enough to look deliberate. DesignPro Academy states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: How DesignPro Academy sequences the first read
editorial.body: One screen, one action, and navigation, the announcement badge and the background clip between them. The brief fixes that order rather than leaving the first screen to a stack of sections. A education reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: The numbers behind the hero section
editorial.body: Almost every decision here is a value you can check: a 800x569 frame. The media is a still at 800x569. The type stays in Inter, so a substitution has to keep the same proportions. Nothing in this hero section depends on a default.

faq.question: What does the brief behind DesignPro Academy actually contain?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 800x569, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: Why does the entry name React and Tailwind CSS at all?
faq.answer: DesignPro Academy was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Where did the DesignPro Academy design come from?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 800x569.
